steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Graf Urtica, Your Excellency, Vyseheim will come to a stop tomorrow at noon. I shall then accompany you to the capital on behalf of Stadtrat Vyseheim.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: I will assist you in investigating this incident.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Furthermore, per protocol, you will be granted freedom of movement within Vyseheim until sundown to make it easier for you to pack your bags and express your goodbyes to those of importance to you.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Of course, considering your special status, as well as the seriousness of this incident, I will personally attend to you throughout your activities in Vyseheim.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Attend me? I expected you to directly say that you're 'surveilling' me.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: (Shrugs)

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: So, where are you planning on going? If possible, please let us know in advance so that––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And if I don't feel like telling you?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Just a friendly reminder - I will be keeping tabs on your every word and action, and my records will greatly affect the outcome of these procedures.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Sure, sure. At this point, I'd rather hear that from some spy or agent. There's a lot more humanity to those types than the likes of you.
Afterglow Hall stands as always, only now, it has fallen silent.
The plaza has thinned out. Only a few casually-dressed people still remain milling about, their eyes full of suspicion.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Please, go easy on me this one time...

steps.name: Plainclothes Guard
steps.text: No.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: This is where Gelais drew his last breath... I just wanted to sing a song he used to enjoy, 'die Melodie für Morgen'...

steps.name: Plainclothes Guard
steps.text: No, get out of here! Music is strictly prohibited in this jurisdiction at the moment. Are you trying to violate the order?!

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: But I'm only going to sing a song. I don't know any Originium Arts...

steps.name: Plainclothes Guard
steps.text: Get out of here right now, or you'll regret it!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Where are you going?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: The guard said commoners aren't allowed in, right? Since I'm a noble, I'll vouch for him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Have you forgotten what happened the last time you brought a commoner into a music store?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: The incident may not have had serious consequences, nor did anyone pursue the matter. Still, one time can be written off as a young man being ignorant and selfish. Two times, and the same can't be said again.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: If you ask me, you've already blurred the line between commoners and nobles in your heart, a line which one must never cross.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Seems like you've calmed down.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: I will make it known in my records that Graf Urtica has come to realize his excessive contact with commoners is one of the main reasons behind the tragedy––

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Your Excellency?!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Ebenholz?

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Err, I mean, Graf Urtica... My apologies, I was too sad to think straight...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Please, don't call me that.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: About Gelais...

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Say no more, I get it. I'm very grateful for your consideration.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: But please, don't finish that sentence. They're all watching, listening.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Oh, right, Herr Czerny is leaving the Afterglow tomorrow. Would you like to go see him?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Czerny? Leaving the Afterglow?

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: You didn't know? He's not doing well, so Hibiscus wants to take him to Rhodes Island for treatment.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Thanks for telling me. I'll go to him right away.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And... my condolences.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Thank you for your kindness...

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: (Sighs audibly)

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Let's get going. And don't make trouble.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'll make trouble for you any day of the week.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You really think you're not making life harder for those Infected? If you really cared about them, you'd keep your distance.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Where've you been all this time? Mr. Czerny and I have been worried half to death about you––

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Don't waste your breath, Hibiscus.
Czerny frowns at the figure standing behind Ebenholz. The noble remains there, motionless.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I heard Czerny was going to leave the Afterglow.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: It's true.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That... isn't something I'd expect of the Czerny I know.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Such is the great Graf Urtica, brandishing his razor wit the moment he steps through the door.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That wasn't meant as an insult.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I know. Since you're here, I'd like to hear what you've been up to since they put you under house arrest––

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Watch your mouth, uncouth peasant.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: ...I'll keep that in mind. Now, might we continue our conversation, o highest of noble lords?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Now then, I'm leaving the Afterglow for three reasons.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: First, my body is in bad shape. Hibiscus was right - my life isn't forfeited yet, and I shouldn't give up my hope for a future just yet.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Is this the same Czerny who used to compose until he vomited blood? Those are some words worth recording.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I don't think those words are very much like me either. Hibiscus is primarily to blame, as she has been forcing these ideas upon me.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Second, I can no longer do anything for the Afterglow as it is now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: What do you mean by that?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The Stadtrat has taken over the entire district. They...

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Ahem–– Ahem.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: ...have been very considerate of us.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The day after the incident, they placed a ban on playing music in public, claiming it was to 'prevent criminal activity.'

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Music stores throughout the Afterglow have been subject to frequent investigation lately, with many of them closing permanently.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I intended to go to have a word with the Stadtrat, but even playing piano in my own home saw them 'politely' breaking into my house. They nearly attacked Ursula last time.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Have they gone mad?!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: If you ask me, they're afraid of––

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Halt your baseless speculation.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Your Excellency, this is not something that should be discussed with commoners.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then, I trust you'll explain the situation in private, good sir.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ignore him, Czerny. What's your third reason?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: That would be the most one. My creative process requires something a bit... different.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: After the incident, I found myself harboring some... more difficult-to-express feelings in my chest.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I need to connect with something different... something brand new, to expand the vocabulary of my music. Perhaps then, I will be able to give voice to a part of those feelings.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That's the first bit of good news I've heard all day.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I wish you the best.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Ebenholz, what are you planning to do next?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Fräulein, I advise you to change the subject.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Um, is there any place you'd like to go?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: An interesting question. How can I go anywhere? Once this city comes to a stop tomorrow...

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Disclosing that is a serious crime.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Well, there you have it.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'll come up with something.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: With what? There is nothing to come up with.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Leaking secrets is a serious crime indeed, and there are thousands of laws in Leithanien. It's a single law I'm managing to not break here.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: My verdict hasn't been handed down yet, so all I can do is wait––

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: This is your last warning, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So, this pretty much sums up the situation.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: There must be a way... I'm sure of it.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Once I'm back at Rhodes Island, I'll go see the Doctor. We'll come up with something, for sure.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Your Doctor is so incredibly capable?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Absolutely.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why would such an incredible Doctor make such efforts for me?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't sell yourself short.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If you weren't the focus of this whole mess, if it was someone else, I can't even imagine what would have become of Vyseheim.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You saw the truth. You stood up to fight. And most importantly, many people... myself included, would have died without your efforts.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Thank you. I truly appreciate your kindness, Hibiscus, but––

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: After your situation settles down, you should come with us to Rhodes Island too.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Me? Go to Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't forget, you're Infected now. You'll need treatment, just like me and Mr. Czerny.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Rhodes Island is a landship. It won't stay in one place for too long, and it doesn't stay on a fixed track. It will cross through many countries, and may even sail to the end of the earth.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Plus, Rhodes Island is huge and has a lot of people onboard.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Remember my sister, Lava? She hates the health food I make just as much, so I'm sure the two of you will have a lot of common ground.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: So... When this is all over, Ebenholz, come to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: ...If I can.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: C'mon, cheer up. Don't start moping already.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Remember what Kreide said to you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Even with how hoarse his voice was––

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You can't forget what he asked of you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: No, I didn't forget... How could I ever forget?!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Then... Try your best to honor his wishes, okay?
Kreide unsteadily shambles to the center of the plaza.
With each step he takes, Originium crystals erupt from his body, his flesh and blood beginning to churn.
A strange melody lingers over the plaza.
The crystals rapidly envelop Kreide's body, transforming into armor, transforming into instruments.
In a heartbeat, the being once known as Kreide is swallowed up, and in his place stands...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (Breathes raggedly)

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I... passed out again?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hibiscus? Hibiscus!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Czerny? Ursula? Where are you?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You're awake, Graf Urtica?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Where's Hibiscus? And Czerny?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: That commoner and his servant have been taken away, along with the Sarkaz woman.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But this is Czerny's house!!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Nay, it is 'a house that shelters them from the wind and rain, by the grace of Their Majesties.'

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: This is for everyone's good. If you had continued your discussion, there's no guarantee that they'd be able to leave Vyseheim tomorrow morning.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You despicable–

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Was there something else you wanted to say?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Nothing I'd say to you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Actually, we came to an agreement earlier. I nearly forgot.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Why isn't the Stadtrat allowing music in the Afterglow?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: It's an edict they decided to issue, nothing more.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I didn't think they'd fly off the handle and pass something like that. Besides, the Afterglow has always paid taxes to Vyseheim. Why would they cut their own revenue like that?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Naturally, to prevent someone from imitating that crime.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If that was true, you wouldn't have snorted in satisfaction earlier when Czerny gave this same excuse.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You'd only feel that way if you knew he had bought into your lies.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let me guess... The Empresses' Voice, right?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: I'd watch myself, if I were you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Seems like I'm right on the mark.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then, I'm assuming some Kurfürsten, like Lehnsfrau Gertrude––

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You... You presumptuous little––!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You're not the best at keeping secrets either, my good sir.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: By the looks of things, he's put a lot of pressure on you. Tell me, what does he think of all this?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Did you come up with this despicable plan because you wanted to exterminate the Infected of the Afterglow without causing a fuss and catching the attention of the Empresses' forces?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Show some restraint! And, I have no idea!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: That's true. Each regional Stadtrat only acts in accordance with what they're told. How would they possibly be able to see through the Kurfürsten's plans?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Are you done yet?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I am.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Then allow me to say something.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Please return to your residence in the Cliffy Patio immediately.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You tried to break into a restricted area, take advantage of a commoner to sow confusion, and discuss confidential information with unauthorized individuals. None of these things will reflect well in your record.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I can't imagine you're doing this with my best interest in mind.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let me guess... Could it be that if your report doesn't look good, it also reflects negatively upon you?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't pretend like you didn't hear me. I know everything in your bag of tricks by now.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Back in Urtica, whenever I got into trouble, I was always most afraid of my own 'agents' and 'attendants.'

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So tell me, how do you people want me to spend the rest of my life? What's the bottom line? Be honest with me, it'll make things easier for both of us.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: (Sighs)

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Just go home. That's the only thing I ask of you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But you said I'm free to go where I please until sunset. Your own words.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Those may be the rules.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: But, those who truly understand the push and pull of these matters will do as I say. They follow the arrangements I lay out for them, and prove that they truly have remorse...

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: And yet you, and that repulsive, unrepentant air you put on like a delusional commoner – nay, like a beast that refuses to be tamed...

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Get a grip already, Graf Urtica.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Listen to me and return to your residence. I'll try to put in a few good words for you in my report.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And if I don't?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Will your report curse me up and down? Will it reveal the terrible job you've been doing?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: (Clicks tongue in anger)

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: They say you're related by blood to the one whose name we dare not speak, and it's clear to me now that the same madness runs in your veins.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So you're finally starting to be honest about me.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Don't get too uppity, boy.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You think I'm afraid of you? You're nothing more than a puppet - what could you possibly know about the art of recording?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: I have a hundred ways to absolve you of responsibility while still keeping you in chains, understand? If you've gotten it through that thick skull of yours, return to your cell!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Sorry, but the sun isn't down yet. I'm free to go wherever I want.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: So keep following me, my cowardly friend. Not that you dare to throw your weight around with an audience.
Ebenholz breaks into a sprint in a narrow alley.
He isn't even thinking about trying to shake off his pursuer.
If he manages to lose him, a new 'tail' will grow back in no time.
If he manages to shake them all, he still has nowhere to go...
Nowhere to go?
Before he knows it, his feet bring him to that place.
Looking at the familiar door and the unfamiliar barricades surrounding it, Ebenholz hesitates.
His 'tail' pants heavily, glaring at him viciously from not too far away. Ebenholz crosses the line of barricades and pushes open the door to the house.
Seeing him disappear through the door, the 'tail' follows him, gasping for breath.
Everything is the same as it was before that performance.
The cups, the dishes, the kettle.
The dirty stovetop, worn furniture, a crude bed, and... a shakedown mat.
Ebenholz suddenly wants to know what it feels like to sleep on it, so he lies down.
Pain. It hurts all over.
The hard ground seems to reject him, putting pressure on every bone in his back.
Just a few seconds makes him feel as if his spine is ready to snap.
The 'tail' glares at him contemptuously as if looking down at a beast, and he returns the same amount of malice.
He's right, anyway. He probably will end up back in chains.
But he's not particularly scared.
He isn't even that curious anymore.
If he were to be honest, he probably has already accepted the vicissitudes of fate.
While other children frolicked beneath the sunlight, he and Kreide learned to remain calm in the face of death.
After struggling to survive through a crazed experiment, one of them became a caged fowlbeast. The other ended up worse-off than an Originium slug in the sewers.
He sought freedom amidst fear, but Kreide was powerless to seek anything beyond food and clothing.
After many years, they finally reunited here.
They decided to work together to put on a concert.
Shouldn't their misfortune have ended here?
After the conclusion of the story, he was supposed to return to his post as a puppet graf, and Kreide was supposed to earn enough money and renown to treat his grandfather.
They were supposed to learn that nobody is ever alone.
But then, they stood upon that stage.
They were ready to give everything for each other.
Generally speaking, such a story should have ended with two earning a new lease on life after making it through all that suffering.
Or, even if fate was meant to torment them, they at least should have perished together, right?
But fate wanted Kreide to die for him. Fate wanted Kreide to die at the hands of the person he intended to give his life for.
Fate wanted Kreide to die, and fate wanted Kreide's death to be meaningless.
Czerny has to leave the Afterglow to seek treatment.
He continues to survive, but will soon go to the capital to face his judgment.
The people of the Afterglow are being strangled, not even permitted to sing a lamentation for their deceased loved ones.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Don't forget what Kreide said to you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You can't forget what he asked of you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Kreide's words––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Have I... forgotten them?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Live on, Ebenholz, and walk through the long night.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Fight injustice, and treat others with generosity and charity.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Only by doing so will I live on in your memory.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'll ask you, how did your day go, Ebenholz?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: And you'll tell me proudly that you had a good and productive day.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: You'll tell me about the challenges you face while doing good, and complain about how fate is a miser.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: And it will be okay, because I'll be listening.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It's alright to complain a little, when you've worked so hard.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Only by doing so will you rise above pain and suffering, and find peace in your heart.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Remember that we've fought together against cruel fate and won.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: When you think of me, laugh. Don't cry.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: So, don't...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Don't go, don't go––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wait!!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Enough!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Huh? You're crying?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Looks like you finally understand the situation you're in.
Ebenholz pulls back a drawer within the room, revealing a solitary cello bow. It is a memento left by Kreide's previous teacher.
Ebenholz carefully wraps up the bow, and takes it with him.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Good sir, do you remember when you first arrived at the scene of the incident? You confiscated my cello. Where is it?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: We're holding on to it, it is an important piece of evidence––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then how come I remember you taking it into Afterglow Hall, dawdling around for a good long while, then coming out empty-handed?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Nonsense. You––

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Get back here! The sun's about to go down! Where do you think you're going?!
The Infected is still there, but he has stopped trying to approach Afterglow Hall.
He stands in the plaza in despair, as if about to be blown away by the wind.
He doesn't even notice Ebenholz's arrival.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: How dare you cross the cordon?! The situation has changed! This is the Empresses' Voice we're talking about now––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You talk too much for a 'tail.'

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You dare draw your wand on me?!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Unfortunately, I don't know any silencing Arts. I'll admit, I'm not as skilled as you in this regard.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But, I can get you to stay put for a while.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Oh, the plainclothes guard is here too?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Good, now nobody will get in the way.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Tell me, Herr Tail, you wouldn't have happened to hide the cello in Afterglow Hall, would you?

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Entry to that area is strictly prohibited. If you think you can get away with––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Unfortunately, there's a cello behind the entrance to Afterglow Hall, quite similar to the one I gave to Kreide.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Hidden in plain view, Herr Tail. I must say, you're quite smart.

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: Put that cello down right now!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Please forgive me.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I don't know what you did with the bow, but... I happen to have a spare.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Alright. This 'die Melodie für Morgen' is for you out there––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Err, no, it's for each and every one of you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (*whispers*) And you too... Kreide.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (*whispers*) I'm not waiting for tomorrow. I'll be complaining to you, just for tonight.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: (*whispers*) I'm going to complain so much you'll grow sick of my annoying voice.

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Is this... 'die Melodie für Morgen'?!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You're committing a crime, Graf Urtica! Do you want to bring even more ruin upon Vyseheim with your Originium Arts?!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: On the contrary, Herr Tail. This is just an ordinary piece of music with no Arts involved.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I will continue to play. I will play the songs of the Infected that you don't want to hear, one by one.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If you don't want to listen, just plug your own ears. Why hold down somebody else's strings?

steps.name: Dispirited Infected
steps.text: Is that... Graf Urtica? He's performing?!

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Graf... Err, Ebenholz!

steps.name: Despondent Infected
steps.text: Ebenholz, thank you! Thank you for your music!

steps.name: Emotional Infected
steps.text: You're amazing, Ebenholz! We're listening; we're all going to keep listening! I'll accompany you––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Wait, you over there, put your instrument down!

steps.name: Emotional Infected
steps.text: Me?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Now that the Stadtrat has explicitly banned non-approved music, I'd recommend you refrain from joining me.

steps.name: Emotional Infected
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This today is just something I decided to do on my own. There's no need to get yourself involved, so just sit back and listen, alright?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Ebenholz?!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: The one who brought music back to the Afterglow... was you?!

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: On behalf of the entire Afterglow, thank you... But please, stop that right now! Your situation is already dire!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I appreciate the concern, but I'm not going to stop.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: This is my performance, and I'm not letting you steal my spotlight!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Calm down and think this through, Ebenholz!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You misunderstand me, Hibiscus.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Didn't you remind me not to forget Kreide's words? It's thanks to you that I finally remembered.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Fate is cruel and unjust, but I was so stricken by grief that I forgot to fight back.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But now, I've remembered.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If there are those seeking to silence the people, then I shall give them a voice.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: If it becomes a crime to pay homage, then I shall offer up a bouquet of fresh flowers.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And if anyone tries to lock me up in a so-called noble spire, then I'll blow the damned thing to smithereens!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You... You've gone too far this time!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Ah, perfect timing, Herr Tail. Please remember to include this in your report!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Unless your verdict is to get rid of me altogether, I'm done with this place!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: And, most importantly, I hereby renounce my noble status!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Nobility is a shame that I can no longer tolerate for even a single day!

steps.name: Aloof Noble
steps.text: You've gone mad! This is unprecedented! You––

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then call me mad! Say I chose the path of madness after long and careful deliberation!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: But now, 'die Melodie für Morgen' is coming to an end, my beloved Infected brothers and sisters!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Let me see your faces, and consider your tastes...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: 'Goldenpokal und Silberbesteck.' If I remember properly, the bearded man in the back liked to hum that song. That'll be the next piece I play.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Then, the third song, 'Winter Wanderlust,' will be dedicated to our tough tailor lady.

steps.name: Familiar Voice
steps.text: The fourth piece, 'Piano Sonata in F-Major, Opus 81, 'An die Freiheit,' is dedicated to you.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Biegler––?!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Alright. As long as I have the skills to adapt that piece for cello, then it'll be the fourth!

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Next up is, 'Goldenpokal und Silberbesteck'! Listen well!
Using his unpolished cello skills, he continues to perform one piece after another.
As if in a frenzy, the gathered Infected begin to weep, laugh, and mourn in the plaza until the Stadtrat rushes to the scene.
He is just like them.
With tears in his eyes, he smiles.
